primary_mathematical_authority.title: Stephen M. Buckley, Space-filling curves and related functions
primary_mathematical_authority.actually_read: Paragraph at PDF lines53–62 explicitly gives continuous surjection of unit interval onto unit square.
primary_mathematical_authority.evidence_limit: Supports existence of a continuous surjection. The loop/compressed-time and discontinuous second-half examples below are our elementary inferences, not quotations or claims made by Buckley.

inference_details.loop: Given continuous surjection P, set Q(t)=P(2t) on[0,1/2],Q(t)=P(2-2t) on[1/2,1]. Then Q is continuous and onto, with Q(0)=Q(1)=o=P(0).
inference_details.pointwise_counterexample: hn(t)=Q(nt) on[0,1/n],hn(t)=o otherwise. Values match at1/n; hn(0)=o. Every fixedt>0 eventually lies after1/n, so hn(t)->o; all stage images still equal the whole square.
inference_details.weak_gloss_counterexample: g(t)=Q(2t) on[0,1/2],g(t)=r on(1/2,1],r!=o. At1/2,g=o but right limit=r. For everyp in square andepsilon>0 choose an interior preimage in first half (the forward/reverse loop gives one even forp=o). Continuity within first half yields a nonempty openI withg(I) inside thep-ball. Thus weak source gloss holds despite discontinuity.
inference_details.positive_sufficient_control: Uniform convergence implies distance(y,h(image))<=distance(y,hn(image))+sup_t||hn(t)-h(t)||. With stage distance tending0 and closed limiting image this proves onto. The supplied pictures alone do not record all required parameter choices.
